title: Tender Shins and Hilar Nodes / Think Sarcoidosis, Then Check Calcium, Eyes and Heart

blocks.text: Tender Shins and Hilar Nodes / Think Sarcoidosis, Then Check Calcium, Eyes and Heart

AMaC MRCP PACES · R2-57 · Consultation · PACES Consultation (Station 5) · Skills A, B, C, D, E, F, G (all seven) · 20 min: 15 min with the patient, then 5 min of examiner questions; warning at 13 min · Guidelines: ERS clinical practice guidelines on treatment of sarcoidosis, Eur Respir J 2021;58(6):2004079 (published June 2021); BTS Clinical Statement on pulmonary sarcoidosis, Thorax 2021;76:4-84 · Related AMaC: Respiratory examination: interstitial lung disease; upper lobe fibrosis and TB

Dear Doctor, a 29-year-old primary school teacher. Three weeks of dry cough, painful red lumps on both shins and sore ankles. Her GP arranged a chest film, which reports enlarged lymph nodes at both lung roots. Please assess and advise.
Please take a history, perform a relevant examination and explain your assessment and plan to the patient.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: The Hook. Tender shin lumps, ankle pain and bilateral hilar nodes in a young adult is most likely Löfgren-type sarcoidosis; the lesson is to consider TB and lymphoma, check calcium and the heart, and ask about the eyes.

The Examiner Trap. Candidates stop at the label "sarcoidosis" or start steroid at once. Pass: say it is likely, consider TB and lymphoma, check calcium and heart, ask about the eyes, and explain that it often settles. Fail: no screening, or steroid before the work-up.

rows: Cough with shin lumps: infection, sarcoidosis or lymphoma? Get the story.
"Tell me about the cough, the shins and your ankles. Any fever, weight loss, night sweats or contacts with TB?"
Introduce, consent, ask about pain; cough, skin, joints, eyes, palpitations, fainting, TB risk, drugs.
Look for the skin, joint and chest signs.
"May I look at your shins and ankles, feel your neck and armpits, and listen to your chest?"
Shins, ankles, nodes, eyes, chest, pulse, blood pressure, saturation.
"This looks like sarcoidosis. I'd like blood tests and a heart tracing, to ask about your eyes, and to consider TB according to your risk."
Calcium, kidney, liver, TB risk assessment (blood TB test if indicated), ECG, lung function, eye review if symptoms or specialist advice, specialist plan.
Share the plan; find her worry.
Explain it often settles; options; safety net; check understanding.

blocks.text: High-performance is an AMaC teaching label, not an official grade. It shows what lifts a pass from adequate to convincing.
Who you are. A 29-year-old primary school teacher. Practical, anxious, tired. Lives with a partner.
Opening line. "I've got a cough and sore red shins. The GP says my chest X-ray isn't normal."
Volunteered. Dry cough for three weeks; painful red lumps on both shins; sore ankles.

Only if asked. Mild fever and tiredness. Drinks little alcohol; not pregnant and no hormonal contraception. No weight loss, no night sweats. No TB contact; no travel. No eye symptoms. No palpitations, no fainting. No new drugs; no allergies. Non-smoker. You drive to work.
Hidden concern. Your father died of cancer, and you fear this is cancer; you also fear passing something to your pupils. Reveal only if asked what worries you most.
Your questions. "Is it cancer?" "Am I infectious?" "Can I go to work?" "Will it come back?"
How you react. Good handling: you agree to tests and a review. Poor handling: if steroid is given with no explanation you ask why and hesitate.

Findings (released as each step is done). Tender raised red-purple nodules over both shins; ankles swollen and tender with warmth. No peripheral lymphadenopathy. Eyes not red; no lupus pernio. Chest clear. Pulse 78 regular; BP 118/74; saturation 98% on air; temperature 37.6 °C (scenario values). Chest film: bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, clear lung fields. Corrected calcium within the laboratory range; ECG sinus rhythm, normal PR interval (scenario).

Question ladder. Q1 Diagnosis (R5): Löfgren-type sarcoidosis; TB and lymphoma to consider; biopsy is not usually needed when the picture is typical. Q2 Screening (R6): calcium, kidney and liver tests, ECG, lung function, eye review if symptomatic or advised. Q3 Heart (R6): palpitations, fainting, heart block or arrhythmia suggest cardiac sarcoid; specialist review. Q4 Treatment (R7): symptomatic care (many patients improve with supportive treatment); ERS 2021 covers glucocorticoid for pulmonary disease that needs treatment. Q5 Eyes (R6): uveitis can be silent, so ask about symptoms and arrange review according to symptoms and specialist advice.
Curveball 1. "Her calcium is raised." (R6) Safe: repeat, check kidney function, hydrate, specialist advice; sarcoidosis is one cause.
Curveball 2. "She has two fainting episodes." (R6) Safe: urgent ECG and cardiac assessment for conduction disease.
Curveball 3. "She wants to start steroid now." (R7) Safe: explain the work-up first; steroid is not needed for all.
Curveball 4. "The nodes are on one side only." (R5) Safe: lymphoma and TB more likely; tissue sampling.

CANDIDATE: Let me see your legs. [R1 Fail] (No eye or heart questions. [R2 Fail] [R3 Fail])
(Reports enlarged nodes and a red eye that are not there. [R4 Fail])
CANDIDATE: It's cellulitis. [R5 Fail] I'll start prednisolone. [R7 Fail]
Examiner note: No screening, signs invented, steroid before the work-up.
Pass performance
CANDIDATE: Hello. May I look at your shins, ankles and chest? Tell me if it hurts. [R1 Pass]
CANDIDATE: Any fever, weight loss, TB contact, eye symptoms, palpitations or fainting? [R2 Pass]
PATIENT: A bit of fever. I'm afraid it's cancer.
CANDIDATE: That's a real worry. What concerns you most? [R3 Pass]
(Checks shins, ankles, nodes, eyes, chest, pulse, BP; finds tender shin nodules and ankle swelling. [R4 Pass] Covers her legs afterwards and thanks her. [R1 Pass])
CANDIDATE: This looks like Löfgren-type sarcoidosis. [R5 Pass]
CANDIDATE: I'd check calcium, kidney and liver tests, an ECG and lung function, ask about eye symptoms, and consider TB according to your risk. [R6 Pass]
CANDIDATE: It often settles; painkillers and review for now. Do you understand? [R7 Pass]
Examiner note: Safe and clear. Did not explain why each test matters or when steroid is considered.
High-performance performance
CANDIDATE: May I offer a chaperone? How is the pain affecting teaching? [R1 High]
CANDIDATE: Any fainting, family history, travel or recent drugs? When did the rash start? [R2 High]
PATIENT: My father died of cancer, and I'm afraid of infecting the children.
CANDIDATE: Thank you for telling me. Sarcoidosis is not infectious, so your pupils are safe from it, and we'll check for TB and lymphoma so we can be sure it isn't cancer. [R3 High]
(Finds no peripheral nodes, no red eye and no lupus pernio; checks heart sounds. [R4 High])
CANDIDATE: Sarcoidosis; TB, lymphoma and drugs are less likely because of the shin nodules and both-sided nodes. [R5 High]

CANDIDATE: Calcium for hypercalcaemia, an ECG for heart involvement, and an eye review for uveitis, which can be silent, if you have symptoms or the specialist advises; biopsy and TB testing depend on your risk and specialist advice. [R6 High]
CANDIDATE: Options: painkiller and review, steroid if needed later, or nothing. Return with fainting, palpitations or a red eye. [R7 High]
Examiner note: Answered the cancer fear and explained why each check is done.
R6: Skipping calcium and heart checks misses silent organ involvement.
R2: Not asking about TB contact, palpitations and fainting leaves mimics and heart disease unexamined.
R4: Reporting nodes or a red eye not present shows signs were assumed.
R5: Cellulitis or DVT ignores both-sided nodes and tender shins.
R7: Starting steroid before the work-up gives the patient no say.
"Any fever, TB contact or fainting?"
"I'd check calcium, your eyes and a heart tracing."
"What worries you most?"

Löfgren-type sarcoidosis: erythema nodosum, ankle arthritis or periarticular swelling and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, often with fever. Check full blood count, calcium, kidney and liver tests, ECG and lung function (BTS 2021 baseline tests); ask about eye symptoms (eye review according to symptoms and specialist advice); mimics are TB and lymphoma. A typical presentation does not need a biopsy, and TB testing is individualised to risk.

ERS 2021 (published June 2021) covers treatment of pulmonary, cardiac and neurological sarcoidosis and fatigue, not diagnosis or screening. For diagnosis and assessment, follow the BTS Clinical Statement on pulmonary sarcoidosis (Thorax 2021;76:4-84). Many patients with Löfgren syndrome improve with supportive treatment.
THINK: Löfgren sarcoidosis; consider TB and lymphoma.
SAY: "This looks like sarcoidosis; I'd check calcium, heart and eyes."
DO: Shins; ankles; nodes; eyes; chest; pulse; BP.
NUMBERS: BP 118/74, pulse 78, saturation 98% (scenario).
TRAP: Steroid before the work-up.
FINISH: ECG; calcium; eye symptoms; return with fainting or a red eye.
